cases.scenario: The sweeping contractor made one trip before the festival and one after it. Both are valid separately paid jobs, and their service dates are recorded.
A replacement employee joined two days after the first issue and received an identical pair. Both were separately purchased at the catalogue price.
Two interpreters worked simultaneously in different rooms and were paid separately at the same rate. The records omit their names and room assignments.
The deposit and balance were separate instalments of the same order, not repeated claims for either instalment. The two instalments have equal amounts and the contract scan is shared.
The same nursery supplied equivalent orders in two planting seasons. Each season was separately invoiced at the fixed contract rate.
Eight defective pairs were returned and exchanged without a new charge. The return credit and replacement invoice each show the full positive merchandise value in the app.
One collection was paid with two separate vouchers because the cash float was split. Each record is for a different voucher amount, although both describe the full item bundle.
A second shelf was added midweek and billed at the same flat minimum as the first shelf. The facility retained the original booking reference for the addition.
The organiser and treasurer describe the one hired cabinet differently. The rental invoice names the same cabinet serial and hire docket in both uploaded copies.
The crew lists these as its only peg purchase for the hill route. Finance has an unattributed cash entry from the same week, but no receipt ties that entry to this crew.

Each workshop bought its own identical set. The purchases used separate receipts, and both workshop names remain in the records.
Two settlements funded separate four-tonne clearances. Their volunteer coordinators used identical text and paid the same agreed rate; settlement names survive only in the scenario log.

The laundry issued a reduced replacement invoice after losing two sheets. Both records concern the one wash, but the earlier form retained the full bill and the later form records the net payment.
The communications desk and logistics desk both entered invoice P-311 for the same print run collected in one box.

The deposit was partly applied against a larger invoice. The final record may be the balance or the full invoice total; neither note states the allocation and the payment ledger is unavailable.
